transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is... I've just stopped wanting to do the things that usually keep me going. 

I don't really know how else to say it, but I just don't have it in me lately. Usually, I'm out doing things—going to salsa nights, church gatherings, or cooking for the neighbors. But I've stopped doing all of that. I don't even want to walk out into my shop just to enjoy the smell of the wood anymore. And I'm a carpenter, so... that's usually my favorite place to be. I just don't have any interest in any of it right now.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah, I have. Most mornings I wake up with this... this heavy, empty feeling right in my chest. It's hard to explain, but it just feels like all the color has completely gone out of the house. I honestly have to force myself not to break down in front of my wife.
Did this start after something particularly stressful happened in your life?

Yeah, it did. It started about two months ago. My wife's health suddenly declined, and... well, our whole daily routine just changed overnight. That's really when this whole change in my mood and how I've been acting started. It's been going on for about two months now.
How has your sleep been lately?
My sleep? Um... I haven't really noticed any changes there, to be honest. I guess I'm sleeping about the same as I always do.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite lately?
No, not really. I mean, I guess I'm still eating my regular meals. I haven't noticed any real change with my appetite.
Have you been worrying a lot more than usual lately?

No, not really. I mean, I'm concerned about my wife, of course, with her health and everything, but I wouldn't say I'm worrying a lot more than usual about other things. Just the normal amount, given the situation.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

Well... I haven't made any plans to hurt myself or anything like that. But I have had thoughts where... where I just think maybe it would be easier if I didn't wake up. And sometimes I catch myself thinking my family might actually be better off without me. It scares me a bit to have those thoughts, to be honest with you, but they have been crossing my mind.
How much is this affecting your ability to manage your day-to-day responsibilities?

It's affecting things a lot, to be honest. At work—I'm a carpenter—I usually supervise the jobs myself, but lately I've had to hand off parts of those jobs to the other guys. I just haven't been able to manage it right now. 

And outside of work... I've pretty much pulled away from everyone. Friends, neighbors, church... I just stopped going or reaching out. It actually got to the point where my wife and our parish contact got worried about my safety, just because of how much I've been isolating myself from everything.
Before your wife’s health declined, had you ever gone through a period like this?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I felt a little down, sure, but nothing like this. This is... this is a lot heavier. I've never felt this low or had these kinds of thoughts before all of this happened with my wife.
Do you feel depressed most of the day nearly every day, even when you're not thinking about your wife's health?

Yes, I do. It's... it's pretty much all the time now. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. It just feels like all the color has gone out of the house, you know? It doesn't really matter what I'm doing or if I'm actively thinking about her health... it's just there. I really have to force myself to hold it together and not just break down crying right in front of my wife.
Have you been feeling worthless lately?

Yeah, I do. Mostly it's... well, I just feel a lot of guilt. I keep replaying every single appointment and every little change in my wife's health in my head. I just keep telling myself that a better husband would have caught it sooner. Like I should have been able to protect her somehow, and I didn't. So, yeah... I feel pretty worthless when I think about that.
Have you been having trouble concentrating lately?

Yeah, I have. It's actually been a real problem at work. I'm a carpenter, and... well, lately I'll just stare at blueprints that I've been reading my whole life, and the lines just kind of blur together in my head. I can't seem to process it. I end up having to ask the younger guys on the crew to repeat things that I should understand right away. It's just really hard to keep my mind on what I'm doing.
Have you been moving or speaking noticeably more slowly than usual lately?

Yeah, the guys at work have actually pointed that out. Sometimes I feel like... like my boots are full of wet cement. It takes me forever just to walk across the shop or bend down to pick up a board. Everything just feels so heavy. But then other times, I get stuck doing the opposite. I'll just be pacing around the shop, rubbing my hands together, not actually getting any work done. It's like I can't settle down, but I'm not moving with any purpose either.
Do these feelings seem stronger than what you would expect from just coping with your wife’s illness?

I... I honestly don't know. I mean, I've never been through something like this before, with her being so sick, so I don't really have anything to compare it to. It's just... it's all pretty overwhelming right now. I couldn't tell you if it's stronger than it should be, or what's normal to expect. I just know I feel awful.
